content.thinking:
I need to plan how the axe is displayed so it touches the floor realistically — maybe mounted upright on a carved ice plinth with its butt-spike seated into the base, matching the real scale of a battle axe with roughly a one-meter haft.

For construction, I'll need one root joint since the builder requires exactly one, and I'm designing the blade asymmetrically: a large dynamic crescent blade extending one direction and a smaller glowing crystal/spike counterweight on the other, with the haft built as a rod using grain-textured paint and a wrapped grip section.

Now I'm working out the crescent blade's outline coordinates relative to the head center, plotting the upper and lower horn tips and the convex cutting edge that bulges outward.

I'll skip a true cutout since subtraction isn't available, instead adding glowing rune and ice-crystal inlays for decoration. I'm marking the two haft-attachment corners as sharp for smoothing purposes, and considering a frost-colored paint highlight along the blade edge.

Writing the paint function...

Writing outline-scaling helper...

For the blade I'm extruding the plate centered on z so it protrudes slightly past the core thickness on both faces, then adding mirrored rune decal planes facing +Z and -Z. I'm sketching a small cyan crescent/snowflake glyph SVG for the rune, sizing viewBox and stroke width proportionally so it scales cleanly at the target render size.

Now for the back spike I'm sweeping a curved ice horn off the haft using a bezier path with a tapering radius and a faceted four-sided cross-section for a crystalline look.

I'm also sketching a glowing crystal cluster at the top of the haft with faceted hex-section spikes, and reworking the overall proportions: setting haft length from ground to about 0.88m, with the blade spanning roughly 0.48 to 1.28m so the axe reads as a believable ~1.3-1.4m weapon.

Now I'm designing the plinth the axe stands on — a lathed ice-block base with a socket for the haft butt, a steel ferrule cap at the bottom, and jagged ice shards leaning outward around the base for visual flair, plus a dusting of snow on top.

I'm adding ice shards scattered around the base as outward-leaning spikes with icy pale coloring, then building the haft as a dark wood-grained rod with wrapped leather grip rings partway up.

For the color palette, I'm going with navy leather wraps accented by cyan glow and gold trim bands at the grip edges and blade collar for a high-contrast, striking look. I'm adding a gold pommel cap and gold socket collars around the head area using short cylinders positioned above and below the head's center.

Then I'm constructing the head mount with a steel langet box where the blade attaches, decorating it with gold trim and gold rivet spheres placed at intervals on the mount faces, and planning jagged frost-like spikes along the cutting edge for texture.

Placing ice spikes outward from the outline points of the blade, computing their direction from the center so they jut naturally off the edge, varying their length randomly and coloring them icy white, extending the effect around the horn tips too.

For the blade's decorative engraving, I'm sketching thin arc sweeps that trace concentric curves around the blade's center, embedding small glowing tubes just above the surface at a shallow depth to look like etched crescent lines along the edge.

Now I'm placing cyan-glowing rune glyph decals near the blade's center, adding octahedron gem accents on the front and back of the mount near the handguard with slight stretching for a faceted gem look, and designing a crystal cluster for the haft's top -- a main spike surrounded by smaller leaning crystals, all resting on a small gold cap cylinder.

I'm giving the crystals a soft icy glow in pale cyan while mixing in a few duller, non-glowing shards for variety, then adding a hanging cloth pennant or tassel that drapes down from the mount's collar with a tapered, curved outline in frosty blue.

Still placing pennant geometry...

Checking floor contact for the ice shards ring around the plinth base—confirming the lowest points sit right at y=0 on the plinth, with shards starting slightly above so nothing clips through. Adding a decorative ring of eight small glowing rune spheres around the plinth's top step for extra detail.

I'm giving the plinth a mottled icy-blue paint treatment, then double-checking my imports to make sure I'm only pulling in what's actually used—THREE, createBuilder, rng, paint, mottle—since unused imports will throw errors.

Setting up the builder for the frost axe with a root joint, then lathing the plinth outline with a defined segment count and icy paint color while being careful not to leave unused variables.

Now I'm defining the haft as a rod with wood texture, color constants for gold and steel, and a mounting box geometry positioned along the handle.

I'm adding gold trim boxes capping the mount, plus ring accents, then looping to build the grip rings with alternating color accents, and finally adjusting the blade's core thickness and outline proportions.

Now I'm scaling the blade's inner edge coordinates relative to a center point so it fits snugly against the mount, then setting up a distance-based gradient function for the core's coloring to create a shaded, layered look.

Adjusting edge thresholds for the blade outline and setting extrusion anchors, then sketching a rune texture SVG with a vertical line, crescent, and snowflake glyph...

Working out the arc radius and placement so it curves nicely around the core without overshooting its edges, trying different center points and angle ranges to keep the geometry contained.

Checking that the glyph fits within the carved-out space between arcs, settling on centering it around x=0.17 with enough width and height to stay clear of the ring boundaries, then setting up the stroke styling with rounded caps and a cyan glow.

Now I'm iterating through the blade edge spike coordinates to build out the jagged silhouette point by point.

Writing spike geometry...

Now for the top crystals, I'm adding a main hexagonal spike with a glow effect, surrounded by four smaller leaning spikes at varied angles and lighter colors, then capping the cluster with a small gold cylinder near the top.

The axe comes out around 1.5 meters tall overall, giving it a heroic scale. I'm adding glowing octahedron gems on the front and back of the mount, small gold rivet spheres at the mount corners, and a glowing cyan rune ring made from a closed catmull-rom circle swept into a thin tube, plus sketching out a plinth step outline beneath it.

Now I'm placing shards jutting out around the base at varied angles with jittered rotation, partially embedding them into the plinth's sloped surface, and considering adding a few squashed white sphere mounds to suggest snow at the base.

Still shaping the pennant outline...
